Discovery must establish existing query conventions, response shape, validation and compatibility expectations; these block the filter and pagination contract. Recorded default if evidence leaves behavior unspecified: preserve existing unfiltered requests, make filtering and pagination opt-in, and follow the project's established conventions; this rules out requiring pagination for existing clients. Assumption: No interactive product or shared cross-session user interaction is requested, so actor identification, hidden state and interaction lifetime are outside this change. The outcome becomes usable through the user-list HTTP endpoint and visible in the source checkout at final return; the isolated checkout remains at its snapshot until then, and any deployed outcome exists only after a release.
